chunks: Ali, from his father, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Hariz, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
When you accompany, so accompany someone like you, and do not accompany the one who suffices (needless) from you, for in that, is humiliation for the Believer.
ai.seo_question: What is the ideal standard for choosing companions in Islam according to the Imams?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS) advises believers to seek companions who are their equals in piety and status, avoiding those who are superior in a way that causes the companion to feel diminished or subservient. This companionship dynamic is described as a source of humiliation (mazzallah) for the believer. In Shia scholarship, this is often interpreted as maintaining spiritual dignity and avoiding excessive deference that might compromise one's own religious standing or self-worth.

en.hubeali:
Ali, from his father, from Hammad Bin Usman, from Hareyz, from the one who mentioned it, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘When you accompany, so accompany someone like you, and do not accompany the one who suffices (needless) from you, for in that, is humiliation for the Believer’.
en.sarwar: 6. Ali has narrated from his father from Hammad ibn ‘Uthman from Hariz from those who he has mentioned who has said the following: “Abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Accompany someone like yourself. Do not accompany one who suffices you; it is humiliation for a believing person.’”
